name: PNB Housing Finance Ltd.
reason: Housing finance company whose EPS fell from INR 58.58 (FY2019) to 31.80 (FY2020) through a credit and governance crisis. It reached 87.80 in FY2026 only with a 10y avg ROE of 11.9% and 6.2%/yr share dilution; earnings are set by the credit cycle and there is no franchise edge.

name: Vardhman Textiles Ltd.
reason: Commodity cotton yarn and fabric spinner: adjusted EPS went from INR 23.89 (FY2016) to 26.20 (FY2026), a 0.9% 10y CAGR. EBIT margin is 7.5% against a 19.5% peak and LTM FCF is negative; cheap but ordinary.

name: CIE Automotive India Ltd.
reason: Cyclical auto forgings and stampings supplier with a 10y avg ROIC of 8.9%. EBIT margin is 10.8% (82nd pctile, avg 8.4%), and it is a low-float subsidiary of CIE Automotive SA; cheap but ordinary with no moat.

name: HDB Financial Services Ltd.
reason: HDFC Bank's retail NBFC (commercial vehicle, consumer and SME loans): EPS fell 61% from INR 12.77 (FY2020) to 4.97 (FY2021) on credit losses. The latest EBIT margin is at its 10y high (100th pctile) and it only listed in 2025; earnings are set by the credit cycle despite good parentage and a 14.2% avg ROE.

name: HDFC Bank Ltd.
reason: India's best-in-class private bank on the US bank standard: adjusted EPS rose from INR 14.27 (FY2017) to 33.37 (FY2022) through the low-rate years and to 48.75 (FY2026), with 9/9 years at or above 7% (worst year +12.2%). 10y avg ROE is 16.6% and consensus FY2/FY3 is +16%; the 2023 HDFC Ltd merger and its deposit and margin dilution are the deep-dive test.

name: Lloyds Metals & Energy Ltd.
reason: Iron-ore miner and sponge-iron/pellet producer whose EPS jumped from INR 2.78 (FY2022) to 66.88 (FY2026) at a record 33.5% EBIT margin (100th pctile); earnings are set by iron-ore prices and LTM FCF is negative on heavy capex.

name: Indraprastha Gas Ltd.
reason: Delhi city-gas distributor partly owned by state firms (GAIL, BPCL): EPS fell from INR 12.48 (FY2024) to 9.72 (FY2026) and EBIT margin is 8.7% against a 17.2% avg after government cuts to cheap administered gas. EV adoption in CNG fleets is a credible 5-yr threat.

name: IndusInd Bank Ltd.
reason: Fails on governance and credit: the 2025 derivative-accounting lapses and microfinance losses cut EPS from INR 114.98 (FY2024) to 11.98 (FY2026), and its 10y avg ROE is 11.2%.

name: City Union Bank Ltd.
reason: Conservative Tamil Nadu MSME and gold-loan bank with no dilution and EPS from INR 4.86 (FY2020) to 13.39 (FY2026). However, EPS fell 31% in FY2020, 10y avg ROE is only 13.0% and long-term growth is 7.5%; like Federal Bank, it is a good regional bank but not best-in-class through the credit cycle.

name: Redington Ltd. (India)
reason: Low-margin IT and Apple distributor with a 2.0% EBIT margin and 10y FCF conversion of 0.37x as working capital absorbs cash. EPS growth from INR 5.73 (FY2017) to 20.07 (FY2026) rests on vendor contracts and Turkey (Arena) exposure; it is commoditised distribution with no specialness.

name: Indus Towers Ltd.
reason: Tower company controlled by Bharti Airtel whose tenancy rests on two customers: EPS swung from INR 7.57 (FY2023) to 37.31 (FY2025, provision write-backs) to 27.09 (FY2026). Vodafone Idea's solvency is a credible single-customer threat and long-term consensus growth is only 4.4%.

name: IDFC First Bank Ltd.
reason: Fails the bank standard: 10y avg ROE is 1.7% and shares grew 14.9%/yr. EPS fell from INR 4.26 (FY2024) to 2.01 (FY2026), and the consensus rebound (+140% FY1) depends on credit costs normalising.

name: Inox Wind Ltd.
reason: Wind-turbine maker that lost money every year from FY2018 to FY2024 (10y avg ROIC -5.7%) and is burning cash (LTM FCF yield -13.8%). It sits inside a complex promoter group with heavy related-party dealings and is at a 16.4% EBIT margin (91st pctile) after the turnaround.

name: Aadhar Housing Finance Ltd.
reason: Blackstone-controlled affordable-housing lender (IPO 2024) whose EPS rose from INR 13.39 (FY2023) to 24.77 (FY2026) with a 16% avg ROE. The pre-FY2021 EPS series is distorted by its DHFL-era restructuring, and there is a short public record, a PE-seller overhang and credit-cycle exposure to low-income borrowers.

name: Power Grid Corp. of India Ltd.
reason: State-owned regulated transmission utility: EPS went from INR 15.11 (FY2022) to only 17.16 (FY2026), about 3%/yr. Long-term consensus growth is 5.9% and returns are set by CERC regulated ROE, so it fails the 7% growth test.

name: UTI Asset Management Co. Ltd.
reason: Market-share-losing mutual fund manager whose earnings track capital markets and treasury gains: EPS was INR 31.57 (FY2017), peaked at 60.20 (FY2024) and was back at 31.40 (FY2026), down 45% in the latest year. It has a 13.8% avg ROIC and no specialness.

name: Capri Global Capital Ltd.
reason: Gold, MSME and housing NBFC with a 10y avg ROE of 10.0% and a 30.5% gap between adjusted and GAAP EPS. EPS fell 36% from INR 9.00 (FY2024) to 5.80 (FY2025); earnings depend on credit and gold prices and there is no franchise edge.

name: Zensar Technologies Ltd.
reason: RPG-group mid-tier IT services firm whose EPS rose from INR 14.43 (FY2023) to 34.39 (FY2026) at a 14.7% EBIT margin (91st pctile). Consensus FY1 is -1.4%, and AI disintermediation of labour-based billing is a credible threat (consistent with EPAM, G and DOX).

name: Apollo Tyres Ltd.
reason: Cyclical tyre maker exposed to rubber and crude input costs, with a 10y avg ROIC of 6.4%. EPS fell from INR 22.57 (FY2016) to 8.31 (FY2020), recovered to 36.93 (FY2026) and has consensus FY1 of -31.4%; cheap but ordinary.

name: Shriram Finance Ltd.
reason: Strong used-commercial-vehicle and MSME lender: EPS rose from INR 11.03 (FY2017) to 53.15 (FY2026) and the worst year was only -6.0% (FY2021). But 10y avg ROE is 14.9%, shares grew 4.9%/yr through the 2022 three-way group merger and new strategic-investor equity, and it relies on wholesale funding through the NBFC credit cycle.
